claims.kickoff_quote: For each track in this wave, name the lane skill that owns its surface in the track's brief and have the implementer use it — python-pro / fastapi-expert / django-expert / postgres-pro / api-designer for backend work, react-expert / nextjs-developer / typescript-pro / vue-expert for web, swift-expert / kotlin-specialist / flutter-expert / react-native-expert for mobile ... Pick from the plugins we actually enabled; a track with no matching lane just uses the core skills.

claims.reasoning: The only KICKOFF mention of nextjs-developer is cross-skill routing: it tells the orchestrator which lane skill owns a track's surface and to hand that assignment down in the track brief. That is selection among sibling skills plus a dispatch/ownership convention — information no individual skill can carry about itself, since a skill's own description only declares its own triggers. Nothing in the block restates the skill's Core Workflow, Constraints, or output template.
